newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Bergsten says risk of dlr getting overvalued.
newsitem.headline: Bergsten says risk of dlr getting overvalued.

text.p: Fred Bergsten, Director of the Institute for International Economics, said on Friday that the dollar was risking getting overvalued.
But he told the World Economic Form that measures being taken by Japan to strengthen its economy were unlikely to reverse the current trend of the U.S. currency.

Bergsten said that the economic fundamentals in the U.S. were so much better than in Japan or Europe that there was no danger of the dollar suddenly going into reverse and falling sharply. "There is no risk of a freefall of the dollar," he said.
Neverthless, the decline of the Japanese yen against the dollar in particular had probably gone too far.

"The yen is far too weak in trade terms thus it will inevitably strengthen," he said. But markets do not take too much notice of the "sustainable levels" of currencies and therefore were unlikely to push the Japanese currency up in the short term, he added.
Earlier, Kosaku Inaba, Chairman of the Japanese Chamber of Commerce and Industry, had told the Forum the current level of the yen was not a concern for Japanese industry.
He said that Japan was used to living with significant swings in its currency's value against the dollar and that the recent drop had not had any psychological impact there.
Inaba said the Japanese economy, while still sluggish, was improving and he did not see any danger of the yen falling very sharply against the dollar. "We don't foresee a freefall," he said.
But he warned that economic reform measures being taken in Japan could take five or six years to have their full impact.
